passages.text: Once again Jesus entered the synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there.
passages.sermon: Jesus entered the synagogue again.\r\nA man was there.\r\nThis man had a withered hand.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπος ἐξηραμμένην ἔχων τὴν χεῖρα

passages.text: In order to accuse Jesus, they were watching to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
passages.sermon: Some people watched Jesus closely.\r\nThey wanted to find a reason to accuse Him.\r\nThey watched to see if Jesus would heal on the Sabbath.
passages.original: καὶ παρετήρουν αὐτὸν εἰ τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύσει αὐτόν ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand up among us.”
passages.sermon: Jesus saw a man with a withered hand.\r\nJesus spoke to the man.\r\nJesus said, “Stand up in the middle.”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ τὴν χεῖρα ἔχοντι ξηράν Ἔγειρε εἰς τὸ μέσον

passages.text: And He asked them, “Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?” But they were silent.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people watching Him.
He asked them a question about the Sabbath.
He said, “Is it lawful to do good on the Sabbath?”
He also said, “Or is it lawful to do evil on the Sabbath?”
He said, “Is it lawful to save a life on the Sabbath?”
He also said, “Or is it lawful to destroy a life on the Sabbath?”
The people did not answer Him.
They remained silent.
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν ἀγαθὸν¦ποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀποκτεῖναι Οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων

passages.text: Jesus looked around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart. Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood among the people in the synagogue.
He saw the Pharisees and others watching Him.
Jesus felt anger.
He also felt sorrow.
He saw that their hearts were hard.
Jesus spoke to the man with the withered hand.
He said, “Stretch out your hand.”
The man stretched out his hand.
His hand became whole again.
God healed him.
passages.original: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος αὐτοὺς μετ’ ὀργῆς συλλυπούμενος ἐπὶ τῇ πωρώσει τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρα σου καὶ ἐξέτεινεν καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: At this, the Pharisees went out and began plotting with the Herodians how they might kill Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees left.
The Herodians were with them.
The Pharisees and the Herodians began to make plans together.
They wanted to find a way to kill Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εὐθὺς μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν συμβούλιον ἐδίδουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν

passages.text: So Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, accompanied by a large crowd from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, the region beyond the Jordan, and the vicinity of Tyre and Sidon. The large crowd came to Him when they heard what great things He was doing.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
Jesus withdrew to the sea.
A large crowd followed Jesus.
People came from Galilee.
People came from Judea.
People came from Jerusalem.
People came from Idumea.
People came from the region beyond the Jordan.
People came from the area around Tyre and Sidon.
The crowd heard about the great things Jesus was doing.
The crowd came to Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀνεχώρησεν πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πολὺ πλῆθος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἠκολούθησεν καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰδουμαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου καὶ περὶ Τύρον καὶ Σιδῶνα πλῆθος πολύ ἀκούοντες ὅσα ἐποίει ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν

passages.text: Jesus asked His disciples to have a boat ready for Him so that the crowd would not crush Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
A large crowd was present.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them to keep a small boat ready for Him.
He wanted the boat because of the crowd.
He did not want the crowd to crush Him.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα πλοιάριον προσκαρτερῇ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μὴ θλίβωσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: For He had healed so many that all who had diseases were pressing forward to touch Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed many people.
Many people had diseases.
These people wanted to touch Jesus.
They pressed forward to reach Him.
They hoped to be healed by touching Him.
passages.original: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐθεράπευσεν ὥστε ἐπιπίπτειν αὐτῷ ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται ὅσοι εἶχον μάστιγας

passages.text: And when the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell down before Him and cried out, “You are the Son of God!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Unclean spirits saw Jesus.
These spirits fell down before Jesus.
They cried out loudly.
They said, “You are the Son of God.”
passages.original: καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα ὅταν αὐτὸν ἐθεώρουν προσέπιπτον αὐτῷ καὶ ἔκραζον λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: But He warned them sternly not to make Him known.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the unclean spirits.\r\nHe warned them many times.\r\nHe told them not to make Him known.
passages.original: καὶ πολλὰ ἐπετίμα αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ αὐτὸν φανερὸν ποιήσωσιν

passages.text: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and called for those He wanted, and they came to Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus went up on the mountain.
Jesus called the people He wanted.
Those people came to Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναβαίνει εἰς τὸ ὄρος καὶ προσκαλεῖται οὓς ἤθελεν αὐτός καὶ ἀπῆλθον πρὸς αὐτόν

passages.text: He appointed twelve of them, whom He designated as apostles, to accompany Him, to be sent out to preach, and to have authority to drive out demons.
passages.sermon:
Jesus chose twelve men.
He called these men apostles.
He wanted them to be with Him.
He sent them out to preach.
He gave them authority to drive out demons.
passages.original: καὶ ἐποίησεν δώδεκα οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν ἵνα ὦσιν μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἵνα ἀποστέλλῃ αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν καὶ ἔχειν ἐξουσίαν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια

passages.text: These are the twelve He appointed: Simon (whom He named Peter), James son of Zebedee and his brother John (whom He named Boanerges, meaning “Sons of Thunder”), Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus chose twelve men.
He called them apostles.
He gave Simon a new name.
He named Simon “Peter.”
He chose James, the son of Zebedee.
He chose John, the brother of James.
He gave James and John a name.
He called them “Boanerges.”
This name means “Sons of Thunder.”
He chose Andrew.
He chose Philip.
He chose Bartholomew.
He chose Matthew.
He chose Thomas.
He chose James, the son of Alphaeus.
He chose Thaddaeus.
He chose Simon the Zealot.
He chose Judas Iscariot.
Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐποίησεν τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα τῷ Σίμωνι Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῖς ὀνόματα Βοανηργές ὅ ἐστιν Υἱοὶ Βροντῆς καὶ Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖον καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν Καναναῖον καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριώθ ὃς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτόν

passages.text: Then Jesus went home, and once again a crowd gathered, so that He and His disciples could not even eat.
passages.sermon:
Jesus went home.
A crowd gathered again.
The crowd was very large.
Jesus and His disciples could not even eat.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς οἶκον καὶ συνέρχεται πάλιν ὁ ὄχλος ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς μηδὲ ἄρτον φαγεῖν

passages.text: When His family heard about this, they went out to take custody of Him, saying, “He is out of His mind.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus had a family.
His family heard about the crowd gathering around Jesus.
They heard that Jesus and His disciples could not even eat because of the crowd.
His family went out to take hold of Jesus.
They wanted to restrain Him.
They said, “He is out of His mind.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξῆλθον κρατῆσαι αὐτόν ἔλεγον γὰρ ὅτι Ἐξέστη

passages.text: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons He drives out demons.”
passages.sermon:
The scribes came down from Jerusalem.
The scribes spoke about Jesus.
The scribes said, “He is possessed by Beelzebul.”
The scribes also said, “He drives out demons by the prince of the demons.”
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβάντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Βεελζεβοὺλ ἔχει καὶ ὅτι Ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια

passages.text: So Jesus called them together and began to speak to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard the scribes accuse Him of casting out demons by Satan’s power.
Jesus called the scribes to Him.
Jesus spoke to them using parables.
Jesus asked them a question.
Jesus said, “How can Satan drive out Satan?”
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Πῶς δύναται Σατανᾶς Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλειν

passages.text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand.
passages.sermon:
A kingdom is a group of people ruled by a king.
If this kingdom fights against itself, it becomes divided.
A divided kingdom cannot remain strong.
That kingdom will fall.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ οὐ δύναται σταθῆναι ἡ βασιλεία ἐκείνη

passages.text: If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.
passages.sermon:
A house is a place where people live together.
A house needs unity to remain strong.
If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.
Division destroys the house.
The house will fall if it is not united.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν οἰκία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ οὐ δυνήσεται ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη σταθῆναι

passages.text: And if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot stand; his end has come.
passages.sermon:
Satan is the enemy of God and people.
If Satan rises up against himself, he becomes divided.
A divided Satan cannot stand.
Satan’s end has come.
passages.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἀνέστη ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἐμερίσθη οὐ δύναται στῆναι ἀλλὰ τέλος ἔχει

passages.text: Indeed, no one can enter a strong man’s house to steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house.
passages.sermon:
A strong man owns a house.
He keeps his possessions there.
No one can enter the strong man's house and steal his possessions.
First, the person must tie up the strong man.
Only then can he plunder the strong man's house.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ οὐ δύναται οὐδεὶς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ εἰσελθὼν τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ διαρπάσαι ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον τὸν ἰσχυρὸν δήσῃ καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει

passages.text: Truly I tell you, the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies, as many as they utter.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said something true and important.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.”
God will forgive the sons of men.
God will forgive all their sins.
God will forgive all their blasphemies.
God will forgive as many sins and blasphemies as they speak.
passages.original: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πάντα ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὰ ἁμαρτήματα καὶ αἱ βλασφημίαι ὅσα ἐὰν βλασφημήσωσιν

passages.text: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He warned them about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
Anyone who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not receive forgiveness.
This person will never be forgiven.
He is guilty of an eternal sin.
passages.original: ὃς δ’ ἂν βλασφημήσῃ εἰς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀλλὰ ἔνοχός ἐστιν αἰωνίου ἁμαρτήματος

passages.text: Jesus made this statement because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke these words for a reason.
Some people said, “He has an unclean spirit.”
They accused Jesus of having an evil spirit.
This accusation led Jesus to make His statement.
passages.original: Ὅτι ἔλεγον Πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον ἔχει

passages.text: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came and stood outside. They sent someone in to summon Him, and a crowd was sitting around Him. “Look,” He was told, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking for You.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was sitting with a crowd around Him.
His mother and His brothers came.
They stood outside the house.
They sent someone to call Jesus.
The messenger spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Your mother and your brothers are outside.
They are asking for you.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔξω στήκοντες ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτὸν καλοῦντες αὐτόν καὶ ἐκάθητο περὶ αὐτὸν ὄχλος καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ζητοῦσίν σε

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “Who are My mother and My brothers?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was sitting with a crowd around Him.
His mother and brothers stood outside.
They sent someone to call Him.
Someone told Jesus, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking for You.”
Jesus answered them.
He said, “Who is My mother?”
He said, “Who are My brothers?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου

passages.text: Looking at those seated in a circle around Him, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat with a crowd around Him.
The people sat in a circle near Jesus.
Jesus looked at the people sitting around Him.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!”
passages.original: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος τοὺς περὶ αὐτὸν κύκλῳ καθημένους λέγει Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου

passages.text: For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people around Him.
He explained who truly belongs to His family.
Anyone who does the will of God is part of His family.
That person is His brother.
That person is His sister.
That person is His mother.
passages.original: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ οὗτος ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν
